text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Demonstrations continue for thirteenth day in Belgrade and other Serbian towns over annullment of local election results. The opposition calls for a commission to be formed to examine the results.
- Association of Independent journalists of Serbia protested against the "unprecedented media blockade" in reaction to jamming of radio station B92 and changing of editorial policy of daily Blic.

- Students address letter to Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic in answer to his accusation that children are being manipulated by the opposition saying "we are not children. We are fully-fledged voters of this community, who ask for respect of laws".

- Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic accuses opposition of acts which are inadmissible in democratic societies. He was reacting to street demonstrations which have continued for almost two weeks.
- Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic recieves high-level delegation of Communist Party of China.

- The Yugoslav proposal for the succession of the former Yugoslavia defines state property as everything that was jointly invested from the federal budget of the former federation and assessing it at some $200 billion, says head of the Yugoslav delegation for succession Kosta Mihajlovic
- Yugoslavia plans to increase export of goods and services by 48 percent in 1997 in relation to 1996, says president of the Yugoslav chamber of economy Mihajlo Milojevic.
- Yugoslavia will have new passports with blue covers from March 1, says federal government.
- The Serbian public prosecutor's office launches investigation against persons who carried out vandal acts during street demonstrations in Belgrade.
- The Belgrade city government says protests threatening vital functions of the city.
- Socialists win majority in third round of local elections according to preliminary results.
- The Serbian Radical Party (SRS) leader accuses the opposition coalition Zajedno of inviting its supporters to take up violence, and criticises them for manipulating children.

- Bosnian Serb Republic decides to withdraw its representative from the arbitration commission of the town of Brcko, saying the commission was trying to impose predetermined solutions to the issue of defining the inter-entity boundary line around the town.
